title: Proper support prevents every relative impurity
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], quasi-coherent modules on small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $Y$ be a scheme and $f:X\to Y$ a finite type quasi-separated morphism, where the finite type and proper properties are [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] and quasi-separated means quasi-compact diagonal. Let $M$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, finite type meaning locally finitely generated on etale scheme charts. Suppose there exist a representable closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], a proper morphism $Z\to Y$, and a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $N$ with $i_*N\simeq M$. This is the proper-support carrier convention of [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Then $M$ is universally pure relative to $Y$ [def-sfb-space-universal-relative-purity].

proof.text: Put $T=\operatorname{Supp}_X(M)$. The finite-type support-pullback theorem makes $T$ closed. Since $M\simeq i_*N$, the closed-pushforward stalk theorem, applied to the underlying abelian sheaf of $N$, makes every geometric stalk of $M$ outside the point image $A=|i|(|Z|)$ zero. Thus $T\subseteq A$. The closed immersion $i$ is proper; by the definition of properness its point map is closed (take the identity base change), so $A$ is closed in $|X|$.

source.place: Tag 0CVI (lemma-proper-pure), reduction to a closed carrier; support closed and vanishing outside the carrier: spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 07TZ, 04E5 and 04XZ.

proof.text: The given closed subspace $Z$ with point set $A$ is proper over $Y$. As $f$ is locally of finite type (it is finite type), the proper-support closed-operations theorem implies first that $A$ is proper over $Y$, and then that its closed subset $T$ is proper over $Y$. Let $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced induced closed subspace on $T$. The same theorem identifies properness of $T$ with properness of $W\to Y$. No factorization of $M$ through a reduced subspace is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tags 0CZC (lemma-closed-proper-over-base) and 0CZE (lemma-closed-closed-proper-over-base), applied to the carrier in Tag 0CVI.

proof.text: Fix any scheme $B\to Y$, write $X_B=X\times_YB$, and let $p:X_B\to X$ be the projection. Put $W_B=W\times_YB=W\times_XX_B$. Proper base change makes $h:W_B\to B$ proper. The reduced-closed-support theorem identifies $|W_B|$ homeomorphically with the closed subset $|p|^{-1}(T)$ of $|X_B|$, without asserting that $W_B$ is reduced. The support-pullback theorem gives that $M_B=p^*M$ is finite type quasi-coherent and $\operatorname{Supp}_{X_B}(M_B)=|p|^{-1}(T)$. Thus $|W_B|$ is exactly the support of $M_B$ as a closed subspace of the point space.

source.place: Tag 0CVI (lemma-proper-pure), universally closed argument; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 04WP and 07TZ, spaces-properties.tex Tag 03IQ and its inverse-image support formulation.

proof.text: Consider a specialization $b^{\prime}\leadsto b$ in $B$ and $\xi\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_B/B}(M_B)$ above $b^{\prime}$, as in the definition of an impurity. That definition gives an etale scheme chart $e:U\to X_B$ and a relative associated point $u$ of the restricted module $M_U$ mapping to $\xi$. By the scheme relative-assassin definition, the stalk of $(M_U)_{b^{\prime}}$ at the corresponding point of the fibre contains a nonzero element whose annihilator is its maximal ideal. Hence $(M_U)_u\ne0$: if this stalk were zero, tensoring it with the fibre local ring would still be zero. The etale-chart support theorem now gives $\xi\in\operatorname{Supp}_{X_B}(M_B)=|W_B|$.

source.place: Tags 0CV8 (definition-impurity), 0CVD (definition-pure); divisors.tex Tag 05AT (definition-relative-assassin) and spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 07TY (lemma-support-covering).

proof.text: Let $w\in|W_B|$ correspond to $\xi$ and put $C=\overline{\{w\}}$ in $|W_B|$. Since $h$ is proper, its point map is closed by the definition of universal closedness at the identity base change. Therefore $h(C)$ is closed in $B$ and contains $h(w)=b^{\prime}$, so it contains $b$. Choose $v\in C$ with $h(v)=b$, and let $\theta$ be its image in $|X_B|$. The closed embedding $|W_B|\hookrightarrow|X_B|$ identifies $C$ with $\overline{\{\xi\}}$: the closure in a closed subspace equals the ambient closure. Thus $\theta\in\overline{\{\xi\}}$ and $f_B(\theta)=b$.

source.place: Tag 0CVI (lemma-proper-pure), final paragraph: the closed image of the closure contains the specialization.

proof.text: The preceding construction works for every scheme $B\to Y$, every $b^{\prime}\leadsto b$, and every relative associated point $\xi$ over $b^{\prime}$. It contradicts the missing-specialization condition of every proposed impurity. By the stated definition, $M$ is universally pure relative to $Y$.
